reason: E1 confirms the formation of a (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4 spinel on the specified alloy under thermal exposure in air, supporting the oxide formation premise. However, it provides no evidence for the dynamic rupture and re-oxidation cycle under sliding wear, nor for the governing balance between formation and rupture, leaving the core mechanistic premises unsupported. E2 is cited as conflicting but addresses a different alloy system and does not directly contradict the hypothesis.
premises: A protective high-entropy spinel oxide (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4 forms on the alloy surface in an oxidizing environment.
Sliding wear mechanically removes this oxide film, exposing fresh substrate.
The exposed substrate re-oxidizes rapidly to re-establish the protective oxide layer.
The balance between oxide film formation and mechanical rupture governs overall degradation.
The alloy composition (20Fe/20Co/20Ni/20Mn/20Cu) is capable of forming this specific spinel oxide.
